sources: EA DSP states WCS exposes raw pixel data such as elevation values.
EA DSP states WCS services are available for LIDAR Composite elevation models.
EA DSP states WCS services use OGC WCS version 2.0.1.
EA DSP distinguishes WCS elevation retrieval from WMS display services.
EA DSP publishes persistent WCS endpoints intended to remain stable across annual composite updates.
EA DSP lists the LIDAR Composite DTM 1m WCS endpoint separately from DSM services.
EA DSP describes WCS as an open non-proprietary replacement for prior image-service access.
The WCS endpoint must be bound to the DTM product, not a DSM or display-only layer.
OGC WCS retrieves digital geospatial information represented as coverages.
WCS Core requirements are mandatory for conformant WCS implementations.
WCS 2.0.1 is an official OGC interface standard version.
WCS extensions separately define scaling, interpolation, CRS and range subsetting behavior.
GeoTIFF coverage encoding is standardized separately from WCS Core.
Scaling is an extension rather than an inherent native-grid identity guarantee.
Interpolation is an extension and therefore must be explicitly controlled when exact source values matter.
Range subsetting can change which coverage fields are returned and must be provenance-bound.
OGC API Coverages examples distinguish native-resolution retrieval from scaled retrieval.
A coverage subset can be requested with a bbox without requesting scaling.
A coverage subset can be requested with axis subset expressions.
scale-size changes the number of cells returned and is non-terminal for native-value identity.
scale-factor can downsample coverage resolution and is non-terminal for exact source pixels.
range/property selection can change returned bands independently of spatial subsetting.
A server may reject very large native-resolution requests; such rejection is not permission to scale terminal data.
Native-resolution spatial subsetting is conceptually distinct from resampling.
GDAL WCS driver opens OGC WCS coverages as raster datasets.
GDAL WCS driver obtains coordinate systems from DescribeCoverage responses.
GDAL WCS driver may issue a small test GetCoverage request while discovering coverage details.
GDAL WCS driver prefers TIFF-containing formats by default when available.
WCS Format or PreferredFormat can be explicitly pinned instead of accepting implicit driver choice.
WCS Interpolation is configurable and only applies when scaling; terminal exact extraction must not request scaling.
WCS BlockXSize and BlockYSize affect remote block caching, not source pixel meaning, but must not change digests.
WCS OverviewCount creates overview representations and cannot be used as terminal exact elevation input.
WCS NoDataValue may be determined by the driver and must be recorded for validity semantics.
WCS Domain selects spatial axes and axis-order handling can apply.
WCS RangeSubset changes coverage fields returned and must be pinned.
WCS Subset trims or slices dimensions and is the appropriate domain-reduction mechanism.
WCS GetCoverageExtra can inject resampling or other server parameters and must be audited.
WCS service responses and metadata are cached by GDAL.
GDAL supports CLEAR_CACHE and REFRESH_CACHE to control WCS cache reuse.
A terminal replay must compare cached and refreshed metadata/coverage identity rather than trusting stale cache.
WCS dataset URL participates in cache keys, so endpoint/version/coverage/range/subset parameters are provenance.
NoGridAxisSwap can suppress otherwise-applied grid axis swapping for server quirks.
SubsetAxisSwap can change boundedBy axis-name ordering in WCS 2.0.1 requests.
Server-specific axis-swap options must never be guessed silently for terminal extraction.
SKIP_GETCOVERAGE can prevent a discovery-time test request but does not replace terminal coverage retrieval.
WCS cache refresh and second-pass retrieval can detect metadata drift between passes.
Additional coverage dimensions require explicit slicing before mapping to a 2D GDAL raster.
BandCount and BandType are normally derived and must be recorded before numeric sampling.
CoverageName is part of the WCS service description and must identify the intended DTM coverage.
The WCS driver can retrieve coverage subsets without requiring a local predownloaded raster.
gdal_translate can subset by exact pixel/line window with -srcwin.
A source window extending outside the raster may be zero-filled unless nodata is defined or error flags are used.
-epo can turn partially-outside source/proj windows into errors instead of accepting fill.
-eco errors only when a requested source/proj window is completely outside.
-projwin subsets in georeferenced coordinates and may expand to pixel boundaries with nearest-neighbor behavior.
-projwin_srs changes coordinate interpretation but does not itself reproject the dataset.
-ovr NONE forces base resolution instead of selecting an overview.
AUTO overview selection may choose a reduced-resolution source closest to target resolution and is non-terminal.
-outsize or -tr can trigger resampling and therefore must be absent from terminal native-value extraction.
-strict can fail on information-losing output conversions and is useful for preservation guards.
-unscale applies band scale/offset and can require an explicit floating output type.
GDAL overviews cover the same geographic region with fewer pixels than the full-resolution band.
Overview selection is software logic and therefore cannot silently substitute for base-resolution terminal pixels.
A raster band may expose arbitrary overviews through gateways capable of remote downsampling.
Remote services that efficiently downsample can still change pixel identity and must remain non-terminal.
GDAL raster resize changes raster dimensions while retaining extent and therefore resamples pixels.
Any resize step is excluded from the terminal exact elevation path.
GDAL reproject can resample when source and destination grids differ.
A resampling factor of one corresponds to no resampling, but terminal extraction avoids warp entirely when source CRS/grid already match.
Chunked warping can yield artifacts or chunk-dependent differences with non-nearest resampling.
Warp error-threshold and chunking options are transformation provenance, not native-pixel identity.
OGC WCS 2.0 conformance testing checks GetCapabilities, DescribeCoverage and GetCoverage behavior.
GetCoverage is a distinct mandatory operation from metadata discovery.
A valid metadata response alone is insufficient evidence that the terminal coverage bytes were retrieved.
Terminal acceptance therefore requires both coverage metadata provenance and the exact returned raster byte/grid/value ledger.
